Camila / Marcus — draft answers below that should map cleanly into the SIG. I've included both short answers for the questionnaire and a couple of supporting details you can paste into an architecture note.

1) Prompt & prompt-log retention (hosted):
- Default: 30 days of full prompt and response logs for hosted API accounts. After 30 days, by default we aggregate telemetry (latency, token counts, error rates) and redact identifiable prompt text; aggregated records are stored for 13 months.
- Customer controls: Hosted customers may shorten retention to 0 days or extend up to 3650 days via a subscription/contract amendment; any extension is addressed on a case-by-case basis with approvals.
- Storage: Logs are stored encrypted at rest in customer-tagged S3 buckets (Redwood-managed for hosted) and access is restricted via IAM roles and audited. In Dedicated/Private, storage remains in the customer VPC or on-prem storage — prompts do not leave that environment unless the customer explicitly requests data export.

2) Use of customer data for training:
- Default policy: Redwood does NOT use customer prompts, responses, or telemetry to train, fine-tune, or improve any models without explicit customer opt-in. The default operating mode for hosted accounts is "no-training" on customer data.
- Opt-in process: Customers who want us to use their anonymized data for model improvement must sign a separate Data Use Addendum that specifies scope, de-identification, retention, and compensation (if applicable). Opt-in is handled via contract plus a service-level flag tied to the customer tenant; opt-in can be revoked with a 30-day notice, and we provide deletion/segregation controls.
- Technical controls: Data used for model improvement is processed in a separate pipeline with limited access, ephemeral credentials, differential privacy tooling where applicable, and removal of PII as required by contract and policy.

3) Dedicated/Private guarantees:
- Dedicated: Prompts and logs are stored in customer-isolated storage tied to the dedicated GPU pool; cross-tenant access is blocked by network and IAM policies. Redwood control-plane signals (for telemetry/health) are minimized and do not contain prompt text.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): By default, no customer data traverses Redwood-managed networks. If customers deploy Redwood Private on their infrastructure, all prompt data and logs remain within the customer's network and storage.

4) Evidence / artifacts we can share:
- Architecture diagram (attached) showing separation between runtime, telemetry, and model-improvement pipelines.
- Excerpted policy text for Data Use (see bullet below) plus a sample Data Use Addendum template (available from legal).

Sample policy excerpt (short):
"Redwood Inference will not use customer-specific prompts, responses, or associated logs to train or fine-tune production models without the customer's explicit, written opt-in. For customers who opt in, data will be de-identified, processed in a separate pipeline, and retained only as specified in the Data Use Addendum."

Notes / caveats:
- We rely on encryption-in-transit and at-rest, access logging, and role-based access controls for auditability (SOC 2 controls).
- For hosted customers, if a regulatory requirement prevents any short-term retention, we can discuss a custom retention/erasure schedule or Dedicated deployment.

If that looks good I can paste a trimmed version back to Nimbus and attach the diagram + sample addendum link.

— Dev

Elena — thanks for the questions. Pulling together the short answers (below) plus the attachments you asked for. I've included an action item list at the end so we can move quickly.

Short answers (for SIG matrix):
- Prompt retention (hosted): Default = 30 days for full prompt/response text; aggregated telemetry kept 13 months. Customer-configurable to shorter/longer windows by contract.
- Use for training: Redwood does NOT use customer prompts/responses for model training without explicit written opt-in (Data Use Addendum).
- Dedicated/Private: Prompts and logs do not leave the customer environment for Dedicated (isolated storage) and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments unless the customer explicitly requests export.
